diagnostic_evidence.quote: Conversely, suppose that $\partial^{\sd}_v f(x)$ exists with the formula \eqref{eq: representation of the specular directional derivative}.
diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: representation of the specular directional derivative

issues.failure_explanation: The converse is false because convergence of the sum of the two transformed difference quotients does not imply convergence of either quotient separately. For example, with $X=\mathbb R$, $x=0$, $v=1$, set $f(0)=0$ and $f(h)=f(-h)=h\sin(\log h)$ for small $h>0$. The right quotient is $\sin(\log h)$ and the left quotient is $-\sin(\log h)$, so neither has an extended-real limit, while the two graph-segment lengths are equal and the specular derivative is identically zero.

diagnostic_evidence.tag: thm: quasi-MVT in normed vector spaces

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis gives only $|g(1)-g(0)|=\|f(v)-f(u)\|$, not the signed equality used in the proof, and a signed quasi-mean-value inequality does not yield the asserted lower bound after taking norms. A scalar counterexample is a continuous piecewise-linear function on $[0,1]$ with slope $10$ on an interval of length $0.1$ and slope $-1$ elsewhere, extended to an open interval. Its endpoint increment is $0.1$, while the absolute specular derivative is $10$ or $1$ off the corner and at the corner equals $\mathcal A(-1,10)=(-11+\sqrt{202})/9>0.1$. Hence the displayed infimum exceeds the endpoint norm.

dependent_affected_formal_result_tags: thm: convergence of the stochastic specular gradient method
issues.failure_explanation: Specular differentiation is nonlinear, so uniform sampling gives the average of the component specular gradients, which need not equal the specular gradient of their average. For instance at zero in one dimension, take $f_1(x)=|x|$ and $f_2(x)=\max(0,x)$. Their specular derivatives are $0$ and $\mathcal A(1,0)$, whereas the derivative of their average is obtained from averaged one-sided slopes and is not their average.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the paper must impose and verify an unbiased estimator condition distinct from uniform component sampling, or redesign the stochastic direction and its analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The stated random-component implementation does not generally satisfy the unbiasedness identity required by the stochastic analysis.
issues.title: Uniform component sampling does not generally produce an unbiased specular gradient
issues.why_classification: The defining stochastic mechanism fails because of the method's central nonlinearity, so repairing it requires a new estimator or a materially narrower function class.

thm: convergence of the stochastic specular gradient method

issues.failure_explanation: In the deterministic proof, $\sum t_k=\infty$ does not directly imply $\sum h_k=\infty$ because $h_k=t_k/\|\nabla^s f(x_k)\|$; the needed boundedness of the gradients along the bounded iterates is never established before the contradiction. In the stochastic proof the defect is stronger: $h_\ell=t_\ell/\|\nabla^s f_{\xi_\ell}(x_\ell)\|$ depends on the sampled index, so it cannot be pulled outside the conditional expectation or combined with unbiasedness of the unnormalized gradient. The expected normalized direction need not be a descent subgradient. Additionally, convergence of a subsequence is incorrectly used as convergence of all iterates in the final deterministic argument.
